The failing test `testHeaderMissingWithNull` in the `CSVParserTest` class of Apache Commons CSV library is encountering a `NullPointerException` when the `CSVFormat` is configured to have an empty header value and a `nullString` of `""`. 

By looking at the `CSVFormat` class, we can see that the default `CSVFormat` object named `DEFAULT` is initialized with certain properties. The `DEFAULT` format does not specify a `nullString`, as it is passed as `null`. When the `withHeader` method is called on a `CSVFormat` object, it sets the header values for the format. Similarly, the `withNullString` method allows setting the string representation for `null` values in the CSV data.

The issue occurs because the `CSVFormat` instance being used does not have a `nullString` specified, and when `withHeader` is called with an empty header value and `withNullString` is set to `""`, it results in a `NullPointerException` as the `nullString` property is not properly initialized.

To fix this issue, the `CSVFormat` object used in the test should be properly configured with a `nullString` value when setting an empty header. This will prevent the `NullPointerException` from occurring.

Next, I will provide the locations that should be fixed in the code:

1. `org.apache.commons.csv.CSVParserTest.testHeaderMissingWithNull(java.lang.String[])`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
